newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty gains capped by c.bank, depos rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty gains capped by c.bank, depos rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty finished today's relatively light trade session nearly unchanged after a late central bank intervention pushed the zloty back under three percent from parity, widely seen as a strong resistance point.

Dealers said the zloty was expected to drift in the narrow range between 2.9 to 3.0 percent from the trading band centre tomorrow and turnover may remain weak as banks were unlikely to sell currencies at more than percent from parity rate.
"The zloty should trade in a narrow range between 2.9-3.0 percent tomorrow after the central bank confirmed three percent as the resistance," said Leszek Szafranek of Bank Slaski SA.
The zloty closed at 2.98/2.88 percent from the trading band centre, virtually unchanged from Wednesday's 2.98/2.75 percent.

It was at 3.0445/75 to the dollar, up from 3.0500/60 on Wednesday and at 1.8075/95 to the mark against 1.8035/80. The central bank bought $6 million at 3.0445 zlotys on Thursday after it purchased some $30 on the market on Wednesday.

Dealers said the zloty briefly strengthened above three percent as banks cut long currency positions opened yesterday amid fears of further central bank action. They said foreign investor entry at today's fixed bond auction would keep the zloty poised for gains ahead of the March 5 value date.

The treasury sold all 200 million zlotys worth of 12-percent five-year bonds on offer on Thursday after investors bid for 346 million. It set the minium price at 80.47, the average price was 80.72 and the maximum price was 81.07.
"The vast majority of accepted bids came from foreign investors," said Arkadiusz Kaminski, the deputy head of the finance ministry's public debt department.
On the money market one-day rates rose after the central bank drained 1.07 billion zlotys through a reverse repo with three repurchase dates, dealers said.
Some dealers also said that monthly tax payments likely pulled up one-day rates as well.
Overnight rates closed at 21.00/21.60 percent, up from opening's 20.50/20.90. Tomorrow/next rates were at 21.00/21.60 percent, alos up from opening's 20.70/21.35 pct.
